private-equity.headline: Capital for your next stage.
private-equity.intro: Explore how equity capital could support growth, an acquisition or a change in ownership.
private-equity.outcomeHeading: What should the next investment make possible?
private-equity.outcomeBody: A useful equity conversation starts with the business plan, the opportunity and the ownership priorities you want to preserve. The structure should follow that discussion.
fit: A defined growth or ownership objective
A business plan and credible financial information
Willingness to discuss ownership and governance
clarify: How much ownership you wish to retain
The role you want an investor to play
Your expected investment and exit horizon
private-equity.mechanics: Equity involves exchanging an ownership interest for capital. Commercial terms, governance rights and future exit expectations need to be assessed together.
useCaseDescriptions: Connect the acquisition plan with the ownership and capital structure it needs.
Consider the investment behind new capacity, markets or capability.
Explore the commercial priorities behind a shareholder or ownership transition.

credit.headline: Finance that moves your business forward.
credit.intro: Explore borrowing options around a clear business need, repayment capacity and practical timetable.
credit.outcomeBody: The right discussion connects the use of funds with the cash flow available to repay them. Existing borrowing, security and flexibility all influence the options worth considering.
fit: A clear funding purpose
Visibility of cash flow and repayment
Information about current facilities
credit.mechanics: Debt provides capital with agreed repayment obligations. The suitability of a structure depends on the requirement, cash generation and the terms a provider is prepared to offer.
useCaseDescriptions: Understand the cash-flow gap behind a contract, trading cycle or growth plan.
Connect expansion costs with a realistic repayment profile.
Review maturity, flexibility and the obligations attached to current borrowing.

ventures.headline: Back the business you’re building.
ventures.intro: Explore the capital conversation behind a new market, a growing team or the next product milestone.
ventures.outcomeHeading: Connect the raise to the next milestone.
ventures.outcomeBody: A convincing funding requirement explains what the capital unlocks, the evidence behind the opportunity and what the business needs to prove next. Stage and investor appetite matter.
fit: A specific milestone and use of capital
Evidence supporting the market opportunity
A view of runway and future funding needs
clarify: Whether the business is ready for external capital
The evidence needed at your stage
ventures.mechanics: Venture funding typically considers growth potential alongside substantial uncertainty. Investment structures, investor involvement and future funding needs deserve attention early.
useCaseDescriptions: Set out the product evidence and resources needed for the next stage.
Connect hiring and sales investment with a defined commercial milestone.
Explain the market-entry plan, runway and evidence behind the opportunity.

real-estate.headline: Turn property ambition into progress.
real-estate.intro: Explore funding around a property purchase, development plan or refinancing requirement.
real-estate.outcomeHeading: Start with the asset and the plan.
real-estate.outcomeBody: A property funding conversation needs more than a purchase price. The asset, ownership structure, timetable, project economics and repayment or exit plan shape the requirement.
fit: An identifiable property or project
A clear use of funds and timetable
Information about the repayment or exit route
real-estate.mechanics: Property finance structures vary with the asset, intended use and project stage. The proposed term and repayment route need to work with the underlying plan.
useCaseDescriptions: Clarify the asset, transaction timetable and proposed ownership structure.
Connect project costs, delivery milestones and the intended exit route.
Review the existing facility against the asset and the next stage of the plan.

special-situations.headline: Find a route through complexity.
special-situations.intro: Explore a capital requirement shaped by change, pressure or an unusual business situation.
special-situations.outcomeHeading: Understand the situation before the structure.
special-situations.outcomeBody: Complex requirements benefit from a clear account of the underlying business, the immediate constraints and the choices available. A realistic timetable and complete information are especially important.
fit: A clearly described situation and objective
Access to up-to-date business information
Decision-makers ready for a candid assessment
clarify: The viability of the proposed plan
special-situations.mechanics: Special situations are assessed individually. The business case, stakeholder position and available capital routes need to be understood before a structure can be evaluated.
useCaseDescriptions: Set out what has changed and the immediate priorities for the business.
Clarify the operating plan, existing obligations and stakeholder position.
Explain the transaction, constraints and decisions that need to align.

life-sciences.headline: Fund the next stage of discovery.
life-sciences.intro: Frame a capital requirement around the evidence, milestones and operating needs of a life-sciences business.
life-sciences.outcomeBody: Funding needs can change considerably between research, development and commercialisation. Explain the milestone, the evidence supporting it and the resources needed to get there.
fit: A defined scientific or commercial milestone
A clear business and funding plan
Relevant technical and financial information
clarify: Capital needs beyond the next milestone
life-sciences.mechanics: Life-sciences requirements depend on the business stage, evidence and intended use of funds. Equity, debt or other routes should be considered in the context of those factors.
useCaseDescriptions: Define the milestone, the supporting evidence and the resources it requires.
Consider the premises, equipment and operating needs behind additional capacity.
Connect the commercial plan with delivery, regulatory and capital dependencies.

tech-opportunities.headline: Make your next capability possible.
tech-opportunities.intro: Explore funding for a defined technology investment, growth plan or infrastructure requirement.
tech-opportunities.outcomeHeading: Link the investment to a business outcome.
tech-opportunities.outcomeBody: Technology is the means, rather than the funding case by itself. Explain what changes commercially, how the investment will be delivered and what supports the capital requirement.
fit: A defined investment and intended outcome
A practical implementation or growth plan
Commercial and financial evidence
clarify: The capital structure that fits the plan
tech-opportunities.mechanics: Technology-related requirements vary between established businesses investing in capability and companies developing technology. The appropriate capital conversation follows the business model and use of funds.
useCaseDescriptions: Define the capability, delivery plan and commercial outcome of the investment.
Connect commercial traction with the people and resources needed to grow.
Explain capacity needs, customer demand and the economics of the infrastructure.

double-impact.headline: Grow with purpose in view.
double-impact.intro: Explore the capital requirement behind a commercial plan with defined social or environmental objectives.
double-impact.outcomeHeading: Define both sides of the ambition.
double-impact.outcomeBody: The commercial case and the intended wider outcome should each be clear. Identify the investment, the practical change it supports and how progress could be measured.
fit: A viable commercial plan
A specific social or environmental objective
A way to evidence the intended outcome
clarify: How the wider outcome will be measured
Whether the requirement fits provider appetite
double-impact.mechanics: An impact-oriented capital conversation considers the business case alongside a defined wider objective. The label alone does not establish suitability or demonstrate an outcome.
useCaseDescriptions: Identify the operational change and the business case supporting it.
Connect the growth plan with a specific, evidenced wider objective.
Define the baseline, the proposed investment and how progress can be assessed.

insurance.headline: Build resilience around your plans.
insurance.intro: Clarify an insurance-related capital requirement and explore the type of specialist conversation it needs.
insurance.outcomeBody: Insurance-related needs can involve different businesses, structures and specialists. Start by distinguishing a capital requirement from a request for insurance cover, then define the commercial objective.
fit: A clearly defined insurance-related business need
Information about the entity and requirement
A view of the relevant constraints
clarify: Whether the need is capital or insurance cover
insurance.mechanics: The required route depends on the entity, purpose and nature of the requirement. A capital conversation should not be confused with advice on, or the arrangement of, an insurance policy.
useCaseDescriptions: Describe the business, growth objective and the capital requirement behind it.
Clarify the financial objective and the specialist constraints that matter.
Set out the transaction, the entity involved and the intended commercial outcome.

crypto.headline: Support the next stage of digital infrastructure.
crypto.intro: Frame a capital requirement around the business model and practical needs of a digital-assets or blockchain business.
crypto.outcomeHeading: Lead with the business behind the technology.
crypto.outcomeBody: A clear requirement explains the operating model, customers, financial position and use of capital. The technology category does not replace a commercial funding case.
fit: A defined business requirement
Transparent operating and financial information
A clear account of the intended use of funds
crypto.mechanics: Digital-asset and blockchain businesses require individual assessment. The capital route depends on the activity, commercial evidence and the providers willing to consider the requirement.
useCaseDescriptions: Explain the infrastructure, its users and the commercial need it addresses.
Connect operating evidence with the capital needed for the next stage.
Define the milestone, the use of funds and the relevant dependencies.
